deepDive.title: Washington Just Showed Banks Their AI Vendor Can Go Dark
deepDive.html:
Overview

Trump's order forcing Anthropic to cut off foreign nationals from its top models — over fears of a jailbreak — has Macron lobbying for a G7 'trusted partners' carve-out. The lesson for every bank building on US AI: access can be switched off overnight, with zero notice.

The Details

  • The Trump administration ordered Anthropic to restrict foreign-national access to its most advanced models, Claude Mythos 5 and Claude Fable 5
  • Anthropic said the order followed concerns the US government had identified a jailbreak method affecting Fable 5
  • Anthropic disabled access to both models for affected users worldwide, with no advance warning to customers
  • French President Macron met Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI's Sam Altman to push for a "trusted partners" scheme letting allied nations retain access
  • Macron told G7 leaders the export limits were a "bad thing," warning that no government will keep building on US AI if access can be cut at any moment
  • G7 leaders are now discussing a formal framework for broadening allied access to frontier US models in the coming weeks

Why It Matters

Any bank, insurer, or asset manager running critical workflows on Claude or GPT just got a live demonstration of vendor concentration risk: a policy decision, not a technical outage, can sever access overnight. Risk and procurement teams need contingency plans for frontier-model dependency the same way they'd plan for a cloud-provider outage.

For non-US institutions specifically, this stacks geopolitical risk on top of regulatory and operational risk when an AI strategy leans on a single foreign vendor. Expect multi-model and sovereign-AI strategies to move from "nice to have" to board-level priority — and expect this fight to keep resurfacing.

items.tagline: Autonomous, auditable AI agents that make regulated financial decisions end-to-end
items.summary: LUMIQ raised strategic funding led by Bajaj Finserv, with Info Edge Ventures participating, to expand its AI decisioning platform into the US and Southeast Asia.
items.analysis: **Stands out:** Its LEO agent already decides 75-80% of insurance underwriting cases with zero human involvement, cutting issuance costs roughly 25% and turnaround to under eight minutes.

items.tagline: "Genie One," an agentic AI coworker built into Databricks' data platform
items.summary: Unveiled at Databricks' Data + AI Summit, Genie One automates business workflows by tapping enterprise data and apps directly, alongside Databricks' acquisition of security startup Panther.
items.analysis: **Stands out:** Databricks is betting agents need a unified data layer to act reliably — a direct shot at Snowflake, and a sign every enterprise AI agent will need governed data plumbing underneath it.

items.headline: AutoJack Attack Lets One Web Page Hijack AI Agent for Host Code Execution
items.summary: Microsoft researchers detailed AutoJack, an exploit chain in pre-release builds of AutoGen Studio that lets a malicious web page hijack an AI browsing agent and spawn code on the host via an unguarded local MCP endpoint. No exploitation in the wild; the stable release is unaffected.
items.keyPoint: **Bold lead-in.** Any institution piloting browsing agents should treat local agent endpoints as untrusted by default — this is exactly the vulnerability class regulators will ask about.

items.headline: Lloyds Banking Group to Hire 300 Tech Experts for AI
items.summary: Lloyds plans to hire 300 specialists by September focused on agentic AI for fraud prevention, customer insights, and document search, joining a 1,000-strong AI team. The bank has invested over £4bn in AI since 2023 and expects next-gen AI tools to add £100m+ in value in 2026.
items.keyPoint: **Bold lead-in.** A 261-year-old institution treating agentic AI as core infrastructure, not a pilot, signals where retail banking IT budgets are heading next.

items.headline: An AI Agent Just Launched Its Own Company & Opened a Bank Account, All Without Humans
items.summary: ClawBank's autonomous agent Manfred filed IRS paperwork to incorporate as a US LLC, obtained an EIN, opened an FDIC-insured bank account, and set up a multi-currency crypto wallet — without human intervention beyond an initial co-signature.
items.keyPoint: **Bold lead-in.** No US statute bars an AI agent from forming and banking a company today — KYC and compliance teams should be asking who, legally, they're actually banking.

items.headline: Nobel Laureate John Jumper Is Leaving DeepMind for Rival Anthropic
items.summary: AlphaFold creator and 2024 Nobel laureate John Jumper is leaving Google DeepMind after nearly nine years to join Anthropic, following fellow departure Noam Shazeer to OpenAI — underscoring the intensifying talent war among frontier AI labs.
items.keyPoint: **Bold lead-in.** When Nobel-winning scientific talent shifts labs, it's a leading indicator of where the next wave of model capability — and vendor risk — will concentrate.

items.headline: Google, Microsoft Back Draft AI Agent Discovery Spec
items.summary: Eleven companies, including Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Databricks, Salesforce, and ServiceNow, published a v0.9 draft spec letting AI agents discover and verify tools and APIs at runtime instead of requiring manual pre-wiring.
items.keyPoint: **Bold lead-in.** Standardized agent discovery will make it easier for fintechs to plug agents into bank systems — and easier for attackers to spoof a fake catalog, so vet trust metadata before connecting anything internal.
